archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A short, mobile passer whose value this year comes from accurate short throws, timely scrambles and avoiding giveaways rather than pushing the ball, with a career-long habit of taking too many sacks.

report.headline: A caretaker with legs who was finding his footing when the hamstring hit.
report.take:
Kyler Murray in Minnesota has been a different quarterback from the Arizona version. The volume and the downfield aggression are gone. His aggressiveness fell from 13% last year to 10.74%, his 2.95-second time to throw is the slowest of his career, and his 170.3 passing yards a game rank 37th of 54. What is left is a passer who completes the short stuff at a high clip, with a 9.8 CPOE on 0-9 yard throws, stays out of trouble (1.9% INT rate, zero fumbles lost), and adds real value with his legs. He is 7th in rushing yards per game, and his 16 scrambles produced 0.599 EPA each and 8 first downs. Paired with the league's No. 1 defense, that has been enough to go 5-1 in his starts, mostly in low-scoring games that went under.

The efficiency numbers are dragged down by a few specific holes more than by the overall quality of his throwing. Throws behind the line cost -13.1 EPA. Those are screens and swing passes, and Aaron Jones's -0.129 EPA per target reflects that dead weight. Third down is worse at -13.4 EPA, with 8.1 yards to go on average and a 36.2% conversion rate. The shotgun-versus-under-center gap is the most telling split: -0.168 EPA a play from shotgun against +0.168 under center. When he is a dropback passer reading the field from the gun, the offense stalls and the sacks pile up. When play-action and the run game set him up, he is efficient. Throws 10+ yards downfield actually grade positively (+0.136 EPA) despite a 42.6% completion rate, so the problem is not arm or nerve.

The sacks are the persistent flaw, and the career says they are who he is. His 8.9% sack rate ranks 38th of 54, and his pressure-to-sack rate is 38.5%. Last year's 0.5 was dead last, and 2019 was 0.378. Holding the ball longer this year to buy scramble lanes makes it worse. The scrambles partly pay for it, but not fully on third down. Before the injury he was trending up. Over his last three games he posted +0.059 EPA per dropback, 7.45 ANY/A and 41.7 rushing yards a game. Those games came against mostly middling defenses, and Detroit's tape showed the aggression creeping back (27.6% aggressive throws, 11.2 intended air yards).

Now the bigger question is the job itself. He is out with a hamstring strain with a projected return of Nov. 29. The depth chart lists him as QB2, and Kirk Cousins started Week 10. He also played only 17% of snaps in Week 1 before Carson Wentz started Week 2. Durability and the depth chart, more than his tape, will decide what his season becomes.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move the chains
strengths.body: His 16 scrambles averaged 0.599 EPA and produced 8 first downs, and his rushing yards per game rank 7th at the position. That is the stable core of his game: he has been a top-12 rusher at the position in every season but last year. It also offsets some of the sack damage. A hamstring strain is exactly the injury that could blunt this on return, so watch his scramble rate early.

strengths.title: Accurate, safe short passing
strengths.body: On 0-9 yard throws he completes 80.3% with a 9.8 CPOE and +8.8 EPA. Overall his CPOE sits 3.3 points above the league average, with a 1.9% interception rate. This is a conservative, timing-based passing profile that suits a team built around its defense. It is sustainable as long as he has reliable underneath targets.

strengths.title: Efficient off play-action looks
strengths.body: Under center he posts +0.168 EPA a play against -0.168 from shotgun. In the red zone he has a 14.9 CPOE and 4 TDs on 21 attempts. When the run game and condensed formations set him up, he hits his throws. That points to a usage fix rather than a skill ceiling, though 39 under-center plays is a modest sample.

concerns.title: Sacks remain a career-long tax
concerns.body: His 8.9% sack rate ranks 38th of 54, and 38.5% of his pressures become sacks. This is not new: last year he converted half his pressures into sacks, and 2019 was similar. Part of it is the price of holding the ball to scramble. Combined with a 2.95-second time to throw, though, it kills drives, especially from shotgun.

concerns.title: Third downs and the shotgun
concerns.body: Third down has cost -13.4 EPA, with only a 36.2% conversion rate on long average distances. Shotgun snaps add up to -21.8 EPA. When the offense needs him to win as a pure dropback passer, it mostly fails. That is partly an offense ranked 30th in EPA and partly his own sack habit, and neither looks likely to change quickly.

concerns.title: Health and the job
concerns.body: He is out with a hamstring strain, is listed as QB2, and Cousins started Week 10. He has started six of nine games and logged only 17% of snaps in Week 1. Even when healthy, a return to the starting role is not guaranteed.

trend.note: After a rough Week 3 at Tampa (-9.2 EPA), each later start was near or above neutral. His last three games ran +0.103 EPA per dropback above his season rate, with more rushing, before the hamstring stopped the climb.

nextGame.headline: Ruled out at San Francisco; Cousins expected to start
nextGame.body:
Murray is listed Out for the Week 11 trip to San Francisco, with a projected return of Nov. 29, so this game is not his. The matchup would actually have suited parts of his profile. The 49ers generate few sacks (31st in sack rate) and are soft on short throws (24th in short-pass EPA allowed), which plays to his underneath accuracy and would ease his sack problem. Their run defense (5th) and deep defense (4th) would squeeze his scrambles and shot plays. The Book has Minnesota as a 3-point underdog against the league's best offense, a script that would have pushed him into the shotgun, dropback mode where he struggles.

The Vikings' receiving corps is also thinned out. Jordan Addison (thumb surgery) and Jauan Jennings are out, and T.J. Hockenson, his most productive target at 0.482 EPA a target, is listed Out but reported as progressing. On the San Francisco side, CB Renardo Green is questionable with a back injury, and DT Gracen Halton is on IR, thinning an already light pass rush. The kickoff forecast, still several days out, calls for drizzle and gusts near 18 mph, which is worth a light hedge on passing.

keyMatchups.title: Weak pass rush versus his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: San Francisco ranks 31st in sack rate. For a passer who takes too many sacks, this is the softest pressure look he could ask for. It matters for his return timeline more than this week, since it shows the matchups where he can be trusted.

keyMatchups.title: Soft underneath, stingy deep
keyMatchups.body: The 49ers allow positive EPA on short passes (24th) but rank 4th against deep throws. That shape aligns with his 0-9 yard strength and away from his low-completion downfield game.

keyMatchups.title: Shootout script against SF offense
keyMatchups.body: The 49ers own the league's top offense, and Minnesota is a road underdog. A trailing script forces more shotgun dropbacks, where Minnesota's quarterbacks have struggled.

nextGame.watch: Whether Murray practices fully this week and whether the Vikings name him or Cousins the starter for Week 12.

restOfSeason.body:
If he reclaims the job after the Nov. 29 target, expect the same low-volume, run-supported shape: modest passing yardage, a low interception rate, and real value on the ground. Minnesota's top-ranked defense keeps games close and pass volume down. The improvement over his last three games is real enough to bank partly, since the short accuracy and scrambling are long-standing traits. The 4.8% TD rate in that stretch is likely to drift back toward his 3.2% season mark. The sack rate won't fix itself; it has followed him for years.

The big caveats are availability and role. A hamstring can linger and sap the scrambling that props up his value. The depth chart lists him second, so a strong Cousins stretch could keep him on the bench. Losing Addison and Jennings for several weeks narrows his options to Jefferson and a hopefully healthy Hockenson. That works for his concentrated, short-area game but caps the ceiling. The ranges below assume he starts.
swingFactors: Whether he regains the starting job from Cousins
Hockenson and Addison returning to health

confidence.note: Six starts, an active hamstring injury and a QB2 depth-chart listing make his role uncertain.
